  nth=18 (frontier array): ret=1 on all ranks
  nth=3..5: bdgraphGatherAll OOM -> MPI_ERRORS_ARE_FATAL abort (PS2-G22-1); nth=0,1: SIGSEGV after 'dgraphGatherAll2: out of memory', nth=2: HANG (dgraphGatherAll2, G18); nth=19: HANG after 'dgraphHaloSync2: out of memory' (G20).
./scan.sh ... 3 1 17 17 -- 4elt.grf 1 'q{strat=f}' 0 1 (baseval 1): 'bdgraph_bipart_sq.c:195:27: runtime error: applying non-zero offset 18446744073709551615 to null pointer' and 'bdgraph.c:158:5: runtime error: applying non-zero offset to non-null pointer 0xffffffffffffffff produced null pointer' (scan_7018_pristine_b1_nth17.txt).
Patched (buildfi): nth=17 baseval 1 -> ret=1 on all ranks, no UBSan report; nth=3..5 -> ret=1 on all ranks (scan_7018_patched_*.txt).
severity_note: Was high in 7.0.17 (hang or SIGSEGV on any single-process allocation failure); 23caa258 made the error handling collective, so what remains is a based NULL pointer (UB, and a non-NULL invalid part array pointer left in the Bdgraph for graphs based at 1).
evidence: bdgraph_bipart_sq.c:191-195: 'if ((dgrfptr->partgsttax = (GraphPart *) memAlloc (...)) == NULL) { errorPrint ("bdgraphBipartSq: out of memory (1)"); reduloctab[5] = 1; } dgrfptr->partgsttax -= dgrfptr->s.baseval;' (basing also on NULL). Fixed by 23caa258: :213 'if ((reduglbtab[4] != 0) && (reduglbtab[4] != dgrfptr->s.procglbnbr)) {' and :219 'if ((reduglbtab[5] != 0) || (reduglbtab[3] != 0)) { goto fail; }' after the MPI_Op_free.
upstream_change: 23caa258be 'Bugfix: read proper array cells for error return codes and improve clean-up on error [report R. Perry]'

upstream_fix_review.details: Right: the failure count and the allocation flag are now read from reduglbtab (sq.c:213, :219), so all processes take the same branch (scan: no hang, no SIGSEGV at nth=6,15,16,17,18); the operator and type are freed before the tests and the centralized graph is freed on every error path through the 'fail' label (sq.c:215). Missing: the part array is still based when its allocation failed (sq.c:195), shown by UBSan with baseval 1; then bdgraphExit (bdgraph.c:158) and any later method that tests 'partgsttax == NULL' see a non-NULL invalid pointer. Behaviour choice: a sequential failure on some processes only is now a fatal 'internal error' in release builds, although the reduction operator (sq.c:98-109) already skips failed processes, and although 5b43f6d2 removed the identical check from the twin vdgraphSeparateSq() as 'useless and bogus': the two Sq twins now behave differently on the same event (extra.json PS3-G22-1). The message 'internal error' is misleading for what is an out-of-memory in a sequential method. The early returns on MPI failures (sq.c:205-207, :210-211) still skip bgraphExit (pre-existing, MPI-fault only).
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Our 7.0.17 0001 did the same global tests, but made the partial-failure check debug-only (as the vdgraph twin then did), freed explicitly on each path, and based the part array only when allocated (else-if chain of bdgraphBipartMlUncoarsen). His goto-fail clean-up is tidier than our repeated bgraphExit; ours is better on the NULL basing and on twin consistency. Rebased: only the basing is kept (0001, 'else' form identical to vdgraphSeparateMlUncoarsen:374-379); the debug-only variant is offered as alt/DMO-03-A-partial-failure-check-debug-only.diff for the user to decide.

review_accuracy: Accurate; its 'Fix:' (test reduglbtab[4], check reduglbtab[5], free what was built) is exactly what 23caa258 did; it did not mention the NULL basing.
first_pass_critique: Correct status, evidence and injections. Its preferred option A kept the unconditional 'internal error' (which is what upstream did) and left 'partgsttax -= baseval' on NULL (still there in 7.0.18). It did not see the bdgraphGatherAll non-collective failures (PS2-G22-1).

evidence: bdgraph.c:193 'grafptr->bbalglbval      = (double) ABS (grafptr->compglbload0dlt) / (double) grafptr->compglbload0avg;'; bdgraph_bipart_sq.c:243 same on dgrfptr; bdgraph_bipart_ml.c:753 '... /* Recompute from best unfolded partition */'; bdgraph_gather_all.c:255 'cgrfptr->bbalval       = dgrfptr->bbalglbval;'.

upstream_fix_review.details: Sets the ratio wherever the partition changes without a method of its own (bdgraphZero :193, bdgraphBipartSq :243, bdgraphBipartMlUncoarsen :753 recomputed instead of copied from the local coarse graph), and gives the gathered Bgraph the distributed value (gather_all.c:255; the early bgraphZero path at :197-201 sets its own). The coarse graph's field is still never written by bdgraphBipartMlCoarsen, but every coarse graph goes through bdgraphZero (Uncoarsen with NULL, ml.c:297-310) or the recomputation (:753) before any strategy reads it, so no uninitialized read remains (probes with fold=d and default sizes clean). The new lines divide by compglbload0avg without the zero guard of bdgraphInit2 (bdgraph.c:138), like the five pre-existing method sites (df :389, ex :493, bd :444, store :174): consistent, only a double inf/NaN if a domain weight were 0. The band copy bdgraph_bipart_bd.c:202 is left, correctly (anchor loads tilt the band graph's own ratio). Cosmetic: df/ex/store keep the explicit ternary while the new lines use ABS.
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Same four sites as our 0004. Ours computed a signed, zero-guarded ratio in bdgraphZero (a leftover of bdgraphInit2's form) and recomputed the gathered value from the centralized loads; his copies the already-correct distributed value and uses ABS everywhere, which is simpler and uniform. His is better; our 0004 is dropped.

review_accuracy: Accurate; understated (garbage coarse value and cross-rank divergence), both resolved by 219040c8.
first_pass_critique: Carried over: probes with default ml parameters could not show the divergence; option B (recompute in bdgraphBipartSt) would not have covered the gathered Bgraph.
